description: AgriSim AI uses NASA Earth observation data and environmental simulations to predict the effects of drought, extreme weather, and soil changes. It recommends sustainable crop rotations and strategies to improve water management, soil health, and agricultural resilience.
summary:
In August 2021 a wildfire burned about 50,000 ha of North Evia, Greece, a third of it farmland. Farmers there now face hotter, drier summers, and erosive autumn storms that hit fields left bare after harvest. AgriSim AI turns free NASA Earth observations into field-level decision support for them.

Field history: for every 30 m field it rebuilds 40 years of crop and fallow history from Landsat.
Sowing check: each week it checks whether conditions favour sowing, using GPM IMERG rainfall, SMAP soil moisture and NASA POWER temperature, and explains why.
Rotations: it compares at least three rotations, the farmer's current one included, with the evidence for each and its risks.
In-season outlook: machine-learning models trained on the satellite record flag, by spring, which fields are on track and which are likely fallow, with honest uncertainty.
Any area: a user can draw a box anywhere. The same pipeline downloads the data, checks whether the rules fit that climate, and trains the area's own models. It ran in full on a second area, in Crete.
It supports the farmer's judgement and never replaces it.
details: AgriSim AI is an AI-powered agricultural decision-support platform that combines NASA satellite data, climate information, and machine learning to help farmers make more sustainable decisions. Using 40 years of Landsat imagery, rainfall, soil moisture, and temperature data, it reconstructs field histories, evaluates sowing conditions, monitors drought and erosion risks, and recommends alternative crop rotations. Built with Python, XGBoost, Streamlit, and FastAPI, the platform provides explainable predictions with uncertainty estimates and allows users to analyze new agricultural areas through an interactive map. Its goal is to improve agricultural resilience, reduce environmental risks, and support smarter farming using free, open Earth observation data.
